subject: Intermittent inference errors & token-lag — Starlight AI (P1)
messages:
From: Carlos Mendez <c.mendez@starlightai.com>

Cc: Sara Lin <sara.lin@starlightai.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T17:02:00-08:00
Subject: Increased 5xxs and sustained token lag across inference cluster

Hi Aisha / Marissa,

We started seeing a sharp increase in 5xx responses and token-level latency this afternoon (roughly 16:45–16:55 PT). Baseline p95 was ~95ms; we're now seeing p95 in the 800–1,200ms range and a 60% drop in sustained throughput for our production routes. Errors are returning as ModelExecutionError and a bunch of client-side timeouts.

Attached two quick artifacts: error-samples.log (recent request/response pairs with headers) and timeline.csv (spike timestamps). This is hitting our checkout and messaging flows — traffic spikes amplify impact. Can you confirm you received and whether this looks like model-side or infra-side?

We can hop on a bridge; Sara and I are available for a sync. This is P1 for us.

Thanks,
Carlos
Carlos Mendez
Head of Platform, Starlight AI
attachments: error-samples.log, timeline.csv

Aisha

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-15T18:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Increased 5xxs and sustained token lag across inference cluster

Quick triage notes (initial):
- Observation: autoscaler created a sequence of short-lived worker pods between 16:40–16:52 PT; some pods failed health checks and were immediately replaced, creating routing churn.
- Telemetry: per-node queue length spiked and KV cache miss rate increased on a subset of pods.
- Hypothesis: rapid scale-up + pod instability caused an imbalance; a percentage of requests hit warm-but-not-ready replicas leading to ModelExecutionError and long cold-start token processing.
- Additional observation: model fallback routing to quantized variant was happening intermittently for routes with >1k tokens.

Immediate actions taken:
- Disabled aggressive autoscaler policy for the affected pool (rollback to conservative scaling).
- Isolated the problematic node image and pulled metrics for 16:30–17:00. Attached node-metrics-11-15.png for the worst-period snapshot.
- Forced a controlled rollout to drain and re-provision healthy replicas.

Recommend: start an exec-level liaison (war-room) to approve temporary capacity bump and rapid rollback window; customer is enterprise and SLA exposure is material.

-Vivek
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
attachments: node-metrics-11-15.png

Subject: Starlight: interim status update (we're on a recovery path)

Carlos / Sara —

Thank you for the quick flag last night. Short, customer-facing summary of the current state and next steps:

What happened (interim):
- Starting ~16:40 PT on 2026-11-15 we observed autoscaler-driven rollout churn that caused a subset of replicas to be briefly unhealthy. That produced routing to warm-but-not-ready replicas and intermittent model fallback for some long-context routes. Result: transient ModelExecutionError responses and elevated token latency.

What we did (actions completed):
- Disabled the aggressive autoscaler policy for the affected pool and forced a controlled rollout to healthy replicas.
- Increased temporary capacity (authorized by Redwood execs) to stabilize throughput while we validate metrics.
- Drained unstable nodes and validated KV cache warmup across the pool.

Current impact:
- Errors have dropped ~80% from peak and p95 token latency is trending down toward baseline. Throughput recovering but not fully back to pre-incident levels.

Next updates:
- We will provide a follow-up update in 60 minutes with metrics and categorical next steps. If we verify full recovery earlier, we'll send that sooner.

Attachments: sla-summary.pdf (interim credit and remediation plan for transparency).

If you'd like to join the ongoing bridge for real-time telemetry, here is the link: https://meet.redwood.ai/bridge/9AB3. Our team is in the bridge now.
